queer_characters.name: Hana / Mark Doda
queer_characters.notes: The source frames Hana/Mark's masculine presentation via the Burrnesha oath as both liberation and constraint, and describes the arc as a 'journey toward wholeness rather than simple transition.' Representation reads as mixed because it centers a culturally specific gender experience while also depicting a return to femininity. I am using the 'queer' umbrella rather than a specific Western label because the source explicitly notes this tradition is distinct from Western trans/nonbinary frameworks.
queer_characters.contest_notes: The source describes the Burrnesha 'sworn virgin' practice as a culturally specific gender-role tradition distinct from Western trans/nonbinary frameworks, and characterizes the arc as rediscovering femininity and reconciling both identities rather than a straightforward transition. Whether this maps onto any specific modern queer or trans identity is genuinely unsettled by the text itself.

contributor_notes: The film centers Hana/Mark, an Albanian woman who takes the Burrnesha (sworn virgin) oath to live socially as a man, later immigrating to Italy and experiencing a 'sexual awakening' and 'forbidden love.' Per Queerview's humility value, I avoided imposing a specific Western identity label since the source explicitly distinguishes the Burrnesha tradition from Western trans/nonbinary frameworks; a maintainer familiar with the film should verify. The gender of the romantic partner in the 'forbidden love' subplot is not specified in the source, so I did not tag same-sex attraction. Audio languages inferred from the 'Albanian/Italian' production note — please confirm. Director Laura Bispuri is named but the source gives no information about her identity, so she is not listed as a queer creator.
